newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks rally, end firm on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks rally, end firm on foreign buying.

text.p: Spurning Wall Street's slide, Chilean stocks closed sharply higher for the fourth day in a row in heavy turnover on foreign buying, but the rally could slow in coming sessions, traders warned.
"The bolsa is likely to rise Thursday, but the gains will be less than today," said Valentin Carril of Santander Investments.
The selective IPSA index closed up 1.66 percent at 109.04 points. The general IGPA index gained 1.23 percent at 5,160.33 points amid volume of 22 billion pesos.
The market continued to be buoyed by hopes that the Central Bank could soon ease its tight credit policy, which has put a brake on stocks for the last year, said dealers.
"There is optimism that the end of the adjustment is close," said one dealer.
A series of figures in recent months pointing to the cooling of the economy have fuelled the rate cut speculation, sparking the bourse's New Year rally.
Bottom-fishing by foreign investors keen to move funds from Wall Street and snap up Chilean stocks badly hammered in last year's sell-off also bolstered the bolsa, said traders.
"They are looking at companies whose steep fall last year is not justified by their long-term outlook," said one trader.
These included pension fund manager Provida, which climbed 6.58 percent to 8,910 pesos.
Other risers included copper products maker Madeco, which rallied on news the company will buy a 67 percent stake in Brazilian cable manufacturer FICAP SA for $121 million.
Madeco ended up 5.42 percent at 1,070 pesos.
Losers included telecom Entel, down 3.06 percent at 2,850 pesos and utility Chilgener, which fell 0.22 percent to 2,300 pesos.
